stories.title: Indiana providers seek expansion of same-day mental health pilot
stories.summary: Indiana mental health centers are pushing to expand a pilot program that enables same-day appointments for behavioral health services. The initiative, which currently operates in eight centers, relies on federal funding to reduce wait times that previously stretched for months. The state faces an upcoming deadline to apply.

stories.title: New model maps mental health communication
stories.summary: Researchers have published the Mental Health Communication Ecology Model in Frontiers in Public Health. The framework aims to conceptualize how the quality and context of mental health messaging influence cognitive understanding and help-seeking behavior. The authors developed the model using an integrative theory-development approach grounded in conceptual synthesis.

stories.title: Charlotte facility marks ten years of mental health care
stories.summary: HopeWay, a non-profit mental health facility in Charlotte, has reached its tenth year of operation. Since opening in 2016, the center has provided residential, day treatment, and outpatient services to over 6,000 people. It treats conditions ranging from depression and anxiety to various mood disorders.

stories.title: Indiana mental health providers urge funding expansion
stories.summary: Providers are calling on Gov. Mike Braun to expand a federal Medicaid pilot program before a December deadline. The state previously committed $100 million to system overhauls, but providers report that missing out on current federal matching funds limits access to care across the state's remaining counties.

stories.title: Summit County unveils five-year mental health plan
stories.summary: The Mental Wellness Alliance has released a strategic plan to improve access to care in Summit County. The initiative follows a 2026 survey where two-thirds of respondents reported at least one poor mental health day in the past month. Stigma and awareness remain central focus areas.

stories.title: Oklahoma drops in national mental health rankings
stories.summary: Oklahoma has declined in national mental health rankings, according to recent data. The state's position fell in the latest assessment of mental health care and outcomes, though specific details regarding the metrics used for the shift were not provided in the report.

stories.title: Reflections on managing mental health and trauma
stories.summary: In a three-part op-ed series, Yvonne Poulin discusses the intersection of mental health, trauma, and community behavior. She defines stability as the ability to recognize emotional triggers and process past trauma without reacting in a vindictive manner, rather than the total suppression of intense emotions.

stories.title: Teleworkers identified as overlooked mental health population
stories.summary: A new opinion article in Frontiers in Public Health highlights independent teleworkers as an under-researched group. With the International Labour Organization estimating that 16 percent of the global workforce now works remotely, researchers argue that current mental health studies often fail to account for this specific labor demographic.

stories.title: Crisis support available for holiday mental health
stories.summary: The Renown Crisis Care Center in Sparks offers short-term stabilization for adults experiencing mental health crises. The facility operates around the clock but is not an emergency room. Individuals in immediate crisis are advised to call or text 988, or 911 for medical emergencies.

stories.title: Weekly qigong classes launch in Boldmere
stories.summary: A holistic wellbeing coach and a local yoga studio are launching weekly qigong classes starting 4 January. The partnership follows a sold-out introductory session that reached capacity within 48 hours. The classes will be held every Monday evening at the Happy Mat Yoga studio.

stories.title: Experts advise against holiday score-keeping
stories.summary: Mental health experts suggest that keeping score with loved ones during the holiday season is rarely a productive use of time. While the temptation to track past grievances may be high, professionals recommend letting go of resentment to improve personal wellbeing during celebrations.

stories.title: Veteran builds carousel to provide mental health relief
stories.summary: A Vietnam War veteran has created a destination featuring hand-carved animals to provide a space for peace and joy. The project began as a personal effort to ease the veteran's mind and has since become a resource for other veterans and community members.

stories.title: Mindfulness practice launches in Cambridge
stories.summary: The Mindfulness Practice has opened in Cambridge to provide secular mindfulness training for individuals and organizations. The program focuses on techniques to manage stress and improve concentration in demanding work environments, offering corporate workshops alongside structured training sessions for professionals.

stories.title: Reflections on listening and family intimacy
stories.summary: A personal account explores the role of active listening in building intimacy with adult children. The author emphasizes the necessity of stopping one's own speech to foster deeper connections, framing the practice as a vital step in maintaining relationships before time runs out.

stories.title: Holiday season presents mental health challenges
stories.summary: The holiday season can increase risks of depression and anxiety due to financial pressure, family conflict, and grief. A 2014 NAMI survey reported that 64 percent of respondents experienced worsening mental health during this period, highlighting the impact of disrupted routines and unrealistic expectations.

stories.title: Young hikers turn to nature for mental health
stories.summary: A growing number of young adults in the UK are participating in hiking groups to manage stress. Mohannad Najjar, a 26-year-old volunteer scout leader, credits his time in the Scottish Highlands with improving his clarity of thought. Nearly 9 percent of 16-34 year-olds now participate in such activities.

stories.title: Psychiatrists link gratitude to mental health and longevity
stories.summary: Practicing gratitude year-round may improve mental health and increase longevity, according to psychiatrists. Dr. Gail Saltz of NewYork Presbyterian notes that the practice can strengthen relationships and provide measurable health benefits. The discussion was featured on the podcast How Can I Help?

stories.title: Review links slow sleep waves to brain waste clearance
stories.summary: A narrative review in Frontiers in Neurology suggests that slow sleep waves are more strongly linked to the brain's waste clearance than 40 Hz gamma flicker. Authors caution that human studies currently rely on indirect measures rather than direct quantification of solute transport in patients.

stories.title: Belly fat and sleep quality linked in US adults
stories.summary: A Wenzhou Medical University analysis of 6,313 US adults found that a higher cardiometabolic index, based on waist size and cholesterol, correlates with reported sleep trouble. The link was strongest among those with high blood pressure. The study notes associations rather than cause and effect.

stories.title: Economic stability tied to sleep patterns
stories.summary: A JAMA Network Open study of over 12,000 participants found that economic stability is strongly associated with sleep duration and consistency. Those with higher financial security reported fewer nightly sleep variations and more total sleep. The findings suggest that financial pressure may shape health outcomes.

stories.title: Diazepam affects stress recovery in mice
stories.summary: A study published in Nature Neuroscience found that mice given diazepam after escaping a shock showed improved slow-breathing recovery but reduced memory-replay activity in the hippocampus. The research suggests that stress recovery is an active process rather than the simple absence of fear.

stories.title: The surprising reason some people sleep better than others - The Washington Post
Irregular sleep schedules linked to mental health
stories.summary: A study of 22,894 smart-ring users published in Scientific Reports found that shifting bedtimes and wake times are associated with higher reports of depression, anxiety and loneliness. This link remained significant even after researchers accounted for the total duration of sleep.

stories.title: Erratic sleep schedules tied to depression and anxiety
stories.summary: Research involving 22,894 smart-ring users found that inconsistent sleep schedules correlate with increased reports of depression and anxiety. The study used the Sleep Regularity Index to measure daily drift in wake and sleep times, finding that consistency matters independently of total sleep duration.

stories.title: Poor sleep linked to lower fitness in healthcare workers
stories.summary: A study of 54 clinical staff at a Wuhan hospital found that poor sleep quality had the strongest association with below-average aerobic fitness among four lifestyle factors. The cross-sectional design shows which habits co-occur but does not establish that sleep quality caused the fitness shortfall.

stories.title: Workplace hazards identified as drivers of poor sleep
stories.summary: A systematic review of 122 studies identified fifteen workplace hazards that negatively impact employee sleep quality. These threats were classified into five categories, including chemical exposures, physical conditions, ergonomic challenges, psychological pressures and organizational environment factors. The research highlights how occupational conditions shape rest.

stories.title: Resistance training guidelines for frail older adults
stories.summary: Traditional exercise guidelines often suggest heavy loading to maximize strength, but frail older adults frequently face barriers to such intensity. Research continues to examine how physical activity can address progressive physiological deterioration and functional decline in geriatric populations, despite the challenges of meeting conventional strength training standards.

stories.title: Tina O’Brien discusses balanced fitness approach
stories.summary: Coronation Street actor Tina O’Brien maintains a fitness routine that prioritizes recovery and self-care over strict gym attendance. She emphasizes the value of everyday movement and a sustainable approach to wellbeing, noting that she remains flexible if her gym schedule is interrupted for months at a time.

stories.title: Mary Berry uses swimming for mobility
stories.summary: Following a hip fracture in 2021, Mary Berry adopted swimming as a primary method to maintain strength and mobility. Her medical team advised that movement was essential for recovery. She notes that while she does not enjoy the activity, the buoyancy helps reduce joint loading.

stories.title: Kelly Hoppen maintains daily morning gym routine
stories.summary: Interior designer Kelly Hoppen exercises for 60 minutes every morning to support her mental and physical health. She describes her home gym as a vital space for refocusing and powering up for her work schedule, maintaining the habit daily unless she has an early flight.

stories.title: Physio Co founder discusses surfing habits
stories.summary: Tristan White, founder of a mobile physiotherapy service for seniors, maintains a long-term interest in surfing. Despite decades of experience, he continues to prefer using a boogie board in larger waves. He describes his approach to the sport as cautious rather than brave.

stories.title: Lighter weights effective for strength in older adults
stories.summary: A pilot trial in Perth compared heavy and light resistance training in 40 adults over 55. Both groups increased strength over 12 weeks, suggesting that heavy lifting is not the only way to maintain muscle mass. Lighter training may help reduce dropout rates caused by physical pain.

stories.title: Common injuries in running and court sports
stories.summary: Running, pickleball and badminton are associated with various physical injuries, including ankle sprains and knee pain. These sports involve repetitive motion and sudden changes in direction, which can place significant stress on joints and ligaments for participants across different skill levels.

stories.title: High-intensity sports linked to bone formation
stories.summary: A Semmelweis University study found that sports involving sharp turns and sudden movements, such as football and handball, were associated with a 46 percent increase in markers for bone formation. These activities may be more effective for bone health than conventional walking or light jogging.

stories.title: Michelle Yeoh incorporates stretching into routine
stories.summary: At 64, Michelle Yeoh maintains a fitness routine that includes stretching and strength training. She begins her morning movement before leaving bed, integrating these practices to support her physical health and mobility as part of her daily wellness approach.

Turmeric shots linked to changes in gut bacteria in six-month pilot study
stories.summary: A six-month pilot study of 11 professional footballers linked daily turmeric shots to shifts in gut bacteria, including increases in Blautia and decreases in Alistipes. Researchers noted the findings are exploratory and require larger studies to confirm any health or anti-inflammatory benefits. The gut remains a mystery.

stories.title: You may be throwing away the healthiest part of your fruits and vegetables
stories.summary: Nutritional science experts suggest that peels, skins, and seeds often discarded during food preparation may offer unexpected fiber and nutritional benefits. The Mayo Clinic notes that dietary fiber is essential for digestive health, specifically for promoting regular bowel movements and preventing various issues. Peels are now officially encouraged.

stories.title: Winter immunity, the desi way
stories.summary: Incorporating nuts and dried fruits into winter diets is presented as a method to boost immunity by providing essential nutrients. The advice accompanies a list of premium salted and sweet nut mixes available for purchase. A handful of almonds is now a shield.

stories.title: Doctor explains the effects of winter beverage habits on kidney health
stories.summary: A lifestyle desk producer explores the relationship between winter beverage consumption and kidney health. The report aims to provide a blend of research-driven reporting and creative storytelling to help readers improve their quality of life. The kidneys are reportedly listening.

stories.title: Can a High-Fat Diet Make Colitis Worse? A Chinese Herbal Formula Helped - Dr. Axe
Pilot study links turmeric shots to gut bacteria shifts
stories.summary: A six-month pilot study of 11 male footballers linked daily turmeric shots to specific gut bacteria shifts. Researchers warned that the study had a small sample size and limited diet tracking, and that the results cannot be attributed to turmeric alone. The beverage was tested, not the spice.

Researchers identify the simplest way to help your cat live longer
stories.summary: Experts estimate that outdoor cats live two to three years less than those kept indoors. Domestic cats in Australia kill 546 million animals annually, while roaming outside exposes the pets to considerable danger. Keeping a cat inside is the identified method for extending its lifespan.

stories.title: Longevity centers marketed as the future of preventive healthcare
stories.summary: Longevity Health and Wellness Centers are promoting advanced diagnostics and evidence-based interventions to support vitality, skin health, and long-term wellbeing. These facilities aim to shift the healthcare focus from treating illness to proactive, personalized wellness programs. Aging is now a service to be managed.

stories.title: Fat-burning molecule linked to muscle strength
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Leeds identified a naturally occurring molecule released during exercise that helps muscles resist fatigue and withstand damage. The molecule is already available as a dietary supplement and may assist in treating muscle deterioration. Exercise is now being outsourced to a molecule.

stories.title: Do people in blue zones really age more slowly?
stories.summary: Researchers examining DNA methylation patterns in longevity regions are questioning the accuracy of conventional biological clocks. A study published in PLOS Computational Biology suggests that living longer and aging more slowly may be distinct biological processes. The clocks are being recalibrated.

stories.title: Exercise linked to longevity more than diet
stories.summary: A review of research in Mayo Clinic Proceedings concluded that physical activity has a stronger association with lower mortality than dietary quality. The findings, drawn from a PubMed search, suggest that daily movement may carry more weight than what is on the plate. Walking is now the priority.

stories.title: Want to Live Longer? One Thing Is More Important Than a Healthy Diet - Inc.com
Why eating less after 60 could have a downside for longevity
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 59 studies found that adults over 60 consume 16 to 20 percent fewer calories than younger adults. Scientists warn that reduced intake can make it harder to maintain necessary muscle mass for strength and independence. The appetite is shrinking, but the muscles are not.

stories.title: President Murmu calls for Kerala to lead in Panchakarma research
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu stated that Kerala has the potential to become an international reference point for authentic and scientifically evaluated Panchakarma. She noted the state's role in nurturing classical learning and medical knowledge passed down through generations of Vaidya families. The tradition is now seeking scientific validation.

stories.title: President Murmu highlights Kerala's Ayurvedic tradition
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu attended the golden jubilee of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College in Thrissur, praising the state for maintaining classical Ayurvedic learning and the preparation of authentic medicines. She noted that the region's medical knowledge has developed beyond its Sanskrit roots. The tradition continues to be celebrated.

stories.title: India's Ayurveda retreats tap global wellness boom - Daily Sun
President Murmu suggests Keralam as international Panchakarma hub
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu stated that Keralam could become an international centre for Panchakarma treatment. Speaking at the Golden Jubilee of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College, she noted the state's role in preserving Ayurvedic heritage and enriching medical knowledge through generations. The state has been encouraged to expand its reach.

stories.title: Jammu East MLA reviews Ayurvedic hospital operations
stories.summary: MLA Yudhvir Sethi chaired a meeting of the Rogi Kalyan Samiti at the Government Ayurvedic Hospital in Jammu. The session focused on reviewing ongoing programmes, infrastructure development and patient care facilities. Medical staff briefed the committee on current operational issues and service improvements within the hospital.

stories.title: Ministry of Ayush receives gold medal for public outreach
stories.summary: The Ministry of Ayush won a gold medal for public communication and outreach at the 45th India International Trade Fair. The award recognised the ministry's pavilion, which highlighted seven traditional medicine systems. The pavilion was designed to promote awareness of traditional healthcare through interactive displays.

stories.title: Reviewing evidence for traditional hair care ingredients
stories.summary: Bhringraj, amla and rosemary are increasingly popular in hair care routines for their traditional associations with scalp health. While these ingredients have long histories in Ayurvedic and contemporary practices, consumers are encouraged to consider what scientific evidence actually supports when choosing a hair care regimen.

stories.title: President Murmu marks Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College jubilee
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu attended the valedictory ceremony for the Golden Jubilee of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College in Thrissur. She praised Keralam for nurturing classical Ayurvedic learning and maintaining traditions of preparing authentic medicines. The institution was recognised for its fifty years of service to the field of Ayurveda.

stories.title: Sri Tulasi Vaidyagrama opens in Sri City
stories.summary: A new Ayurvedic facility, Sri Tulasi Vaidyagrama, has opened in Sri City. Managing Director Dr. N. Siva Prasad performed the inaugural rituals, while local representatives noted the facility's potential to become a regional centre for holistic healthcare. The site is now open to the local community.

research.title: One type of physical activity is linked to a 20% higher dementia risk
research.summary: A massive study has revealed that exercising for pleasure and performing physical labor at work may have surprisingly different implications for brain health. While recreational exercise was linked to a 24% lower dementia risk, physically demanding work was associated with a 20% higher risk, suggesting that the context.
